physical_harm: The deceased was shot dead and suffered injuries from blows with 'gandasas' (axes) and a knife
number_of_offences: Six offences/counts charged, five were finally upheld
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the statements of the eye-witnesses PW7 and PW8, but noted that the version of events provided by PW7 regarding the appellants preventing people from entering the shop was an addition to the original complaint and not fully established.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the credibility of the main witnesses (PW7 and PW8) as brothers of the deceased, but found their statements inconsistent and questionable, particularly regarding the involvement of the appellants in the assault.
bail_history: Appellants are on bail, their bail bonds shall stand discharged

legal_representation.accused: V. Giri, Sr. Adv., Mrs. Kawaljit Kochar, Ms. Krishna Parkhari, Ms. Kusum Chaudhary
legal_representation.state: Anish Kumar Gupta, AAG, Chandra Shekhar Suman, R. K. Rajwanshi, Ms. Deepshikha Bharati, Dr. Monika Gusain

investigation_status: First Information Report registered, complaint made by PW7 on the date of occurrence, evidence collected from PW7 and PW8

appeal_history.trial_court: Conviction of appellants under sections 148, 302, 342, 452 read with section 149 of the Penal Code

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellants were standing in the street and preventing people from entering the shop and moving on the street in front of the shop at the time of the occurrence, and that they were involved in the assault which resulted in the death of the deceased.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the appellants were not involved in the assault which took place inside the shop, that the statements of the prosecution witnesses were false, and that the appellants were innocent family members roped in due to enmity.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the principle that the prosecution must prove its case beyond a reasonable doubt and that the benefit of doubt should be given to the accused when there is doubt about their involvement.
